subject: Copywriting
title: Just Do It: Three Words, Billions
description: A fast breakdown of Just Do It: Three Words, Billions for builders.

hook.text: In 1988, Nike was losing to Reebok. Dan Wieden wrote three words that turned it around: 'Just Do It.'

buildup.text: Wieden said the phrase was inspired by a death row inmate's last words: 'Let's do it.' He changed 'let's' to 'just.'

discovery.text: The line worked because it wasn't about shoes. It was about overcoming hesitation. Universal and timeless.

twist.text: Nike's sales went from $877M to $9.2B in ten years. Three words generated more value than any product feature.

climax.text: Every great tagline transcends its product. 'Just Do It' could sell anything. That's the mark of perfect copy.

punchline.text: Three words. $877M to $9.2B. That's a tagline.

quiz.question: What was Nike's revenue before 'Just Do It'?
